source_text: –Τί οὖν σεαυτὸν ἐξαπατᾷς, νῦν μὲν κακῶς εἰς ἀπόλαυσιν σαρ κὸς τὸν πλοῦτον διατιθέμενος, ἐπαγγελλόμενος δὲ εἰς ὕστερον ὧν οὐκέτι ἔσῃ κύριος; Ὡς ὁ λόγος ἔδειξε, πονηρὰ ἡ βουλή· ζῶν μὲν, ἀπολαύσω τῶν ἡδονῶν· ἀποθανὼν δὲ, πράξω τὰ διατεταγμένα. Ἐρεῖ καὶ σοὶ Ἀβραάμ· Ἀπέλαβες τὰ ἀγαθά σου ἐν τῇ ζωῇ σου· Οὐ δέχεταί σε ἡ στενὴ καὶ τεθλιμμένη ὁδὸς, τὸν ὄγκον τοῦ πλούτου μὴ ἀποθέμενον. Βαστάζων αὐτὸν ἐξῆλθες· μὴ γὰρ ἀπέῤῥιψας, ὡς προσετάχθης. Ὅτε ἔζης, σεαυτὸν τῆς ἐντολῆς προετίθεις· μετὰ τὸν θάνατον καὶ τὴν διάλυσιν, τότε τὴν ἐντολὴν τῶν ἐχθρῶν προετίμησας. Ἵνα γὰρ μὴ λάβῃ ὁ δεῖνα, λαβέτω, φησὶν, ὁ Κύριος. Καὶ τοῦτο τί εἴπωμεν, ἐχθρῶν ἄμυναν, ἢ τοῦ πλησίον ἀγάπην; Ἀνάγνωθί σου τὰς διαθήκας. Ἐβουλόμην μὲν ζῇν, καὶ ἀπολαύειν τῶν ἐμαυτοῦ. Τῷ θανάτῳ χάρις, οὐ σοί. Εἰ γὰρ ἦς ἀθάνατος, οὐκ ἂν ἐμνήσθης τῶν ἐντολῶν· Μὴ πλανᾶσθε· Θεὸς οὐ μυκτηρίζεται· Νεκρὸν εἰς θυσιαστήριον οὐκ ἀνάγεται· ζῶσαν προσένεγκε τὴν θυσίαν. Ὁ ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύματος προσφέρων ἀπρόσδεκτος. Σὺ δὲ ἃ μετὰ πᾶσαν τὴν ζωὴν ἐπερίσσευσε, ταῦτα προσφέρεις τῷ εὐεργέτῃ. Εἰ οὐ τολμᾷς ἐκ τῶν λειψάνων τῆς τραπέζης δεξιώσασθαι τοὺς ἐνδόξους, πῶς οὖν τολμᾷς τὸν Θεὸν ἐκ τῶν λειψάνων ἐξιλεοῦσθαι; Ἴδετε τὸ τέλος τῆς φιλοχρηματίας, οἱ πλούσιοι, καὶ παύσασθε ἐμπαθῶς πρὸς τὰ χρήματα διακείμενοι. Ὅσῳ φιλόπλουτος εἶ, τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον μηδὲν ὑπολίπῃ τῶν προσόντων σοι. Πάντα σεαυτοῦ ποίησαι, πάντα ἐπικόμισαι, μὴ καταλίπῃς ἀλλοτρίοις τὸν πλοῦτον. Τάχα σε οὐδὲ περιστελοῦσιν οἱ οἰκέται τῷ τελευταίῳ κόσμῳ, ἀλλ' ἀφοσιώσονται τὴν ταφὴν, τοῖς κληρονόμοις λοιπὸν προσχωρήσαντες κατὰ τὴν εὔνοιαν. Ἤ που καὶ καταφιλοσοφήσουσί σου τότε· Ἀπειροκαλία, φησὶν, καλλωπίζειν νεκρὸν, καὶ πολυτελῶς ἐκκομίζειν τὸν οὐκέτι αἰσθανόμενον. Τί δὲ οὐ βέλτιον τοὺς περιόντας κοσμεῖσθαι τῇ πολυτελεῖ καὶ ἐνδόξῳ περιβολῇ, ἢ συγκατασήπειν τῷ νεκρῷ τὰ πολυτίμητα τῆς ἐσθῆτος; Τί δὲ μνήματος ἐπισήμου, καὶ ταφῆς πολυτελοῦς, καὶ δαπάνης ἀκερδοῦς ὄφελος; Δέον εἰς τὰ κατὰ τὸν βίον ἀναγκαῖα χρήσασθαι τοῖς περιοῦσιν. Τοιαῦτα ἐροῦσι καὶ σὲ τῆς βαρύτητος ἀμυνόμενοι, καὶ τοῖς διαδεξαμένοις τὰ σὰ χαριζόμενοι. Προλαβὼν οὖν, σεαυτὸν ἐνταφίασον. Καλὸν ἐντάφιον ἡ εὐσέβεια. Πάντα περιβαλλόμενος ἄπελθε· οἰκεῖον κόσμον τὸν πλοῦτον ποίησαι· ἔχε αὐτὸν μετὰ σεαυτοῦ. Πείσθητι καλῷ συμβούλῳ, τῷ ἀγαπήσαντί σε Χριστῷ, τῷ δι' ἡμᾶς πτωχεύσαντι, ἵνα ἡμεῖς τῇ ἐκείνου πτωχείᾳ πλουτήσωμεν· τῷ δόντι ἑαυτὸν λύτρον ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν. Ἢ ὡς σοφῷ τὸ συμφέρον ἡμῖν συνορῶντι πεισθῶμεν, ἢ ὡς ἀγαπῶντος ἡμᾶς ἀνασχώμεθα, ἢ ὡς εὐεργέτην ἡμῶν ἀμειψώμεθα. Πάντως δὲ ποιήσωμεν τὰ διατεταγμένα ἡμῖν, ἵνα κληρονόμοι γενώμεθα. τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς τῆς ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ Χριστῷ· ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
orientation: Basil is closing the homily, directly addressing the rich who plan to leave their wealth to the poor only after death.
pass_a_gloss: Why then do you deceive yourself, now indeed badly disposing the wealth for enjoyment of flesh, but promising for later things of which you will no longer be master? As the word showed, evil is the plan: while living, I will enjoy the pleasures; but when I have died, I will do the things commanded. Abraham will also say to you: You received your good things in your life. The narrow and afflicted way does not receive you, the one who has not put off the bulk of wealth. Carrying it you went out; for you did not throw it away, as you were commanded. When you were living, you were putting yourself before the commandment; after death and dissolution, then you preferred the commandment to your enemies. For in order that so-and-so may not take it, let the Lord take it, he says. And this what shall we call it, defense against enemies, or love of neighbor? Read your wills. I was wishing to live, and to enjoy my own things. Thanks to death, not to you. For if you were immortal, you would not have remembered the commandments. Do not be deceived; God is not mocked. A corpse is not brought up to the altar; bring the sacrifice living. The one who offers from the surplus is unacceptable. But you offer to the benefactor the things that after the whole life were left over. If you do not dare to entertain the distinguished from the leavings of the table, how then do you dare to appease God from the leavings? See the end of love of money, you rich, and stop being disposed passionately toward possessions. By as much as you are a lover of wealth, by so much more leave nothing of the things belonging to you. Make all things your own, carry all things with you, do not leave the wealth to others. Perhaps the household servants will not even wrap you in the final adornment, but they will perform the burial as a mere formality, henceforth attaching themselves to the heirs according to their goodwill. And surely they will then lecture you: It is tastelessness, they say, to adorn a corpse, and to carry out expensively the one who no longer perceives. And why is it not better for the survivors to be adorned with the expensive and glorious clothing, than for the precious things of the garment to rot together with the corpse? And what is the benefit of a conspicuous tomb, and expensive burial, and profitless expense? It was necessary to use for the necessities of life for the survivors. Such things they will say, both defending themselves against your severity, and gratifying those who inherited your things. Anticipating therefore, bury yourself. A good burial garment is piety. Clothed with all things depart; make the wealth your own adornment; have it with yourself. Obey the good counselor, Christ who loved you, who became poor for us, in order that we by his poverty might become rich; who gave himself as a ransom for us. Either as a wise one seeing what is beneficial for us let us obey, or as one loving us let us endure, or as our benefactor let us repay. In every way let us do the things commanded to us, in order that we may become heirs of eternal life in Christ himself; to whom be the glory and the might forever and ever. Amen.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the genitive phrase; 'flesh' is kept as the source's stark term for bodily pleasure, not softened to 'the body' or 'sensual pleasure.'
ὄγκος means bulk or weight; 'bulk' preserves the image of wealth as a heavy burden that blocks the narrow way.

choices.english: they will perform the burial as a mere formality
choices.why: ἀφοσιόομαι means to discharge a duty perfunctorily or as a formality; the rendering captures the servants' minimal, duty-only care.
rejected: they will perform the burial out of obligation

choices.why: The imperative is literal and startling; 'bury yourself' keeps the paradox of preparing one's own burial through giving, rather than softening to 'prepare your burial.'
The compound verb means to speak philosophically at or against someone; 'lecture you' captures the ironic, condescending tone of servants moralizing over the corpse.
ἀνέχομαι means to endure or bear with someone; 'let us endure' keeps the sense of patient submission to one who loves us.

pass_b_english: Why then do you deceive yourself, spending your wealth badly now on the enjoyment of flesh, while promising for later what you will no longer be master of? As the word has shown, the plan is wicked: While I live, I will enjoy pleasures; when I die, I will do what has been commanded. Abraham will also say to you: "You received your good things in your life" (Luke 16:25). The narrow and afflicted way does not receive you, since you have not put off the bulk of wealth. You went out carrying it; for you did not throw it away, as you were commanded. While you lived, you put yourself before the commandment; after death and dissolution, then you preferred the commandment of your enemies. "So that so-and-so does not get it," he says, "let the Lord take it." And what shall we call this—revenge on enemies, or love of neighbor? Read your wills. "I wanted to live and enjoy my own things." Thanks belong to death, not to you. For if you were immortal, you would never have remembered the commandments. Do not be deceived; God is not mocked (Galatians 6:7). A dead thing is not brought to the altar; bring a living sacrifice. The one who offers from surplus is unacceptable. But you offer to your benefactor what was left over after your whole life. If you do not dare to welcome honored guests with the leftovers from your table, how then do you dare to appease God with leftovers? See the end of love of wealth, you rich, and stop being so passionately disposed toward possessions. The more you love wealth, the more you should leave nothing of what belongs to you behind. Make everything your own; carry everything with you; do not leave your wealth to strangers. Perhaps your servants will not even wrap you in your final adornment, but will perform the burial as a mere formality, having already shifted their loyalty to the heirs. Indeed, they will then lecture you: "It is vulgar," they say, "to beautify a corpse and to carry out with great expense one who no longer feels anything." Is it not better for the living to be adorned with costly and glorious clothing than for the precious garments to rot together with the corpse? What good is a conspicuous tomb, an expensive burial, and profitless expenditure? One ought to use what remains for the necessities of life for the living. Such things they will say, avenging themselves on your harshness and gratifying those who inherit what is yours. So act first, and bury yourself. Piety is a fine burial garment. Wrap yourself in everything and depart; make your wealth your own adornment; keep it with you. Be persuaded by the good counselor, by Christ who loved you, who became poor for our sake so that we might become rich through his poverty (2 Corinthians 8:9), who gave himself as a ransom for us (1 Timothy 2:6). Let us be persuaded by him as one wise who sees what benefits us, or let us endure him as one who loves us, or let us repay him as our benefactor. In every way let us do what has been commanded us, so that we may become heirs of eternal life in Christ himself; to him be glory and power forever and ever. Amen.

problems.quote: after death and dissolution, then you preferred the commandment to your enemies
problems.source_quote: μετὰ τὸν θάνατον καὶ τὴν διάλυσιν, τότε τὴν ἐντολὴν τῶν ἐχθρῶν προετίμησας
problems.why: Wrong agency: you preferred the commandment OF your enemies, not TO your enemies.
problems.fix: after death and dissolution, then you preferred the commandment of your enemies.

problems.quote: What is needed is to use what remains for the necessities of life
problems.source_quote: Δέον εἰς τὰ κατὰ τὸν βίον ἀναγκαῖα χρήσασθαι τοῖς περιοῦσιν
problems.why: Wrong sense: 'δέον' = 'it is necessary/one ought,' not 'what is needed'; 'χρήσασθαι τοῖς περιοῦσιν' = to use the surplus things, not 'what remains for necessities of life'.
problems.fix: One ought to use the surplus for life's necessities.
problems.ruling: τοῖς περιοῦσιν = 'the surplus/remaining things' (dative object of χρήσασθαι), not 'what remains for necessities'; mistranslates syntax.

edits.old: after death and dissolution, then you preferred the commandment to your enemies
edits.new: after death and dissolution, then you preferred the commandment of your enemies

edits.old: What is needed is to use what remains for the necessities of life
edits.new: One ought to use the surplus for life's necessities

fixed: Corrected 'to your enemies' to 'of your enemies' to match the source genitive 'τῶν ἐχθρῶν'.
Corrected 'What is needed is to use what remains for the necessities of life' to 'One ought to use the surplus for life's necessities' to match 'Δέον... χρήσασθαι τοῖς περιοῦσιν'.

problems.quote: One ought to use the surplus for life's necessities
problems.source_quote: Δέον εἰς τὰ κατὰ τὸν βίον ἀναγκαῖα χρήσασθαι τοῖς περιοῦσιν
problems.why: τοῖς περιοῦσιν means 'the living/survivors,' not 'the surplus.' The duty is to use wealth for the living.
problems.fix: One ought to use what remains for the necessities of life
problems.ruling: τοῖς περιοῦσιν is dative plural of οἱ περιόντες ('the living/survivors'), not τὰ περισσεύοντα ('surplus'); meaning changed from helping living people to using leftover wealth.

problems.ruling: ζῶν μὲν...πράξω is the rich man's wicked plan (ἡ βουλὴ), not Scripture; quotation marks mislead readers.

last_rejected.quote: make your wealth your own adornment
last_rejected.why: Source says 'make wealth your own adornment' but context means make it truly yours by giving it away; 'adornment' misses the point.
last_rejected.ruling: κόσμον means 'adornment' (LSJ); 'make wealth your own adornment' is within normal range. Contextual theology claim is interpretation, not translation error.

last_rejected.quote: So act first, and bury yourself.
last_rejected.why: Προλαβὼν means 'anticipating/acting before death,' not just 'act first.' The urgency of acting before it's too late is lost.
last_rejected.ruling: Προλαβὼν commonly means 'to anticipate, act first'; 'So act first' captures the temporal urgency adequately. Not a major meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: "So that so-and-so does not get it," he says, "let the Lord take it."
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἵνα γὰρ μὴ λάβῃ ὁ δεῖνα, λαβέτω, φησὶν, ὁ Κύριος
last_rejected.why: English makes rich man speak, but Greek φησίν refers to the testament/will's wording, not direct speech by the rich man.
last_rejected.fix: "So that so-and-so does not get it, let the Lord take it," says the will.
last_rejected.ruling: φησίν is ambiguous; 'he says' can represent the will's wording. Not a clear mistranslation.

last_rejected.quote: then you preferred the commandment of your enemies
last_rejected.source_quote: τότε τὴν ἐντολὴν τῶν ἐχθρῶν προετίμησας
last_rejected.why: Greek says you preferred the enemies' commandment, not 'commandment of your enemies' as a phrase; the enemies' command is what you obeyed.
last_rejected.fix: then you preferred the commandment given by your enemies
last_rejected.ruling: 'commandment of your enemies' correctly renders τὴν ἐντολὴν τῶν ἐχθρῶν; claim is a distinction without difference.

last_rejected.quote: perform the burial as a mere formality
last_rejected.why: ἀφοσιόομαι means to discharge as a duty minimally or perfunctorily, but 'mere formality' loses the sense of grudging, minimal compliance; 'go through the motions' or 'discharge perfunctorily' better.
last_rejected.fix: will go through the motions of the burial
last_rejected.ruling: 'mere formality' captures ἀφοσιώσονται's sense of perfunctory discharge; a preference, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: having already shifted their loyalty to the heirs
last_rejected.source_quote: τοῖς κληρονόμοις λοιπὸν προσχωρήσαντες κατὰ τὴν εὔνοιαν
last_rejected.why: κατὰ τὴν εὔνοιαν means 'in accordance with goodwill/favor' or 'to show favor,' not 'shifted their loyalty'; servants transfer their goodwill to heirs, not loyalty.
last_rejected.fix: having transferred their goodwill to the heirs
last_rejected.ruling: 'shifted loyalty' reasonably renders προσχωρήσαντες κατὰ τὴν εὔνοιαν; within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: gratifying those who inherit what is yours
last_rejected.why: χαρίζομαι means to gratify or do a favor, but context suggests servants are currying favor with heirs, not 'gratifying' them; 'currying favor with'.
last_rejected.fix: currying favor with those who inherit your things
last_rejected.ruling: 'gratifying' is valid for χαριζόμενοι; 'currying favor' is a nuance preference, not a meaning change.
